body.statement:
Consider a stationary independent binary-endpoint experiment with predictable sequential randomization, logged propensities satisfying \(\pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha}\) and \(\pi_t(0)\geq\varepsilon\), and potential delays satisfying \(P\{D_t(a)>u\}\leq\min\{1,L(1+u)^{-\beta}\}\).  The armwise risk difference is the causal contrast \(\tau=P Y_t(1)-P Y_t(0)\).  From records observed through \(H_T=T+\Delta_T\), compute \(\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}\) and its intervals as defined above.  Uniform asymptotic honesty of the unpadded ordinary-Wald interval \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\) over the one-sided policy class \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\) requires
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad q=(1-\alpha)/2.
\]
On the regular subclass \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), this condition is also sufficient for ordinary Wald.  Without the regular-variance condition, the uniformly honest choice is the measurable hybrid \(I_{T,\Delta}\), which uses the bias-aware Gaussian interval only on the observable gate \(G_{T,\Delta}\) and otherwise uses the concentration interval; with the same quota-failure convention, the concentration interval may instead be used alone.  With no extra follow-up, the displayed condition holds when \(\beta>q\).  When \(\beta=q\), it holds if and only if \(\Delta_T/T\to\infty\); when \(\beta<q\), it holds if and only if \(T+\Delta_T\gg T^{q/\beta}\).  Necessity is class-wide rather than pointwise: prompt-delay laws with \(b_{T,\Delta}=0\) may admit ordinary-Wald inference.  The hidden-tail witness used for the tail necessity deliberately permits outcome--delay dependence, whereas the separate sampling-rate converse is compatible with outcome--delay independence.
body.proof_tex:
For a binary endpoint, \(Y_t(a)\in\{0,1\}\subset[-1,1]\).  The stationary independent sampling and predictable randomization conditions in the statement, together with
\[
 \pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha},\qquad \pi_t(0)\geq\varepsilon,
 \qquad P\{D_t(a)>u\}\leq\min\{1,L(1+u)^{-\beta}\}, \tag{1}
\]
place the experiment in \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\).  No rare-arm upper bound is used.  Moreover,
\[
 PY_t(1)-PY_t(0)=P\{Y_t(1)=1\}-P\{Y_t(0)=1\}=\tau, \tag{2}
\]
so the risk difference is the causal potential-outcome contrast.

Measurability and unconditional coverage follow from \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}gated\text{-}inference}\).  Explicitly, assignments determine tape order and \(E_T\); recorded revelation times determine the two truncation indicators; an absent response contributes zero once its guaranteed age exceeds the relevant threshold; and quota failure produces \([-2,2]\).  For the concentration branch, independence of the fixed tape prefixes gives
\[
 P\left\{\left|(M_{1,\Delta}-PM_{1,\Delta})
 -(M_{0,\Delta}-PM_{0,\Delta})\right|>\sqrt{2S_Tx}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-x}, \tag{3}
\]
and boundedness plus the tail envelope give, for each arm,
\[
 P\left\{|U_{a,\Delta}-PU_{a,\Delta}|>
 \sqrt{\frac{2v_{T,\Delta}x}{J_a}}+\frac{4x}{3J_a}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-x}. \tag{4}
\]
The old-cohort identity is
\[
 P\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}=\tau-b_{T,\Delta},qquad
 |b_{T,\Delta}|\leq B_{T,\Delta}. \tag{5}
\]
Taking \(x=\log(6/\eta)\) in (3)--(4) and applying a union bound proves coverage at least \(1-\eta\) on quota success; the full interval on quota failure proves unconditional coverage.  The gated theorem supplies the corresponding uniform hybrid guarantee and its regular-subclass Gaussian approximation.

We prove necessity of the ordinary-Wald condition within binary outcomes.  Set
\[
 x_T=T^q(1+H_T)^{-\beta},\qquad
 \delta_T=\min\left\{\frac14,\frac L2(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\right\}, \tag{6}
\]
and use \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\).  For \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), let \((r_1^\sigma,r_0^\sigma)=(1,0)\) if \(\sigma=1\), and \((0,1)\) if \(\sigma=-1\).  Independently over arrivals, define
\[
 (D(a),Y(a))=
 \begin{cases}
 (H_T+1,r_a^\sigma),&\text{with probability }\delta_T,\\
 (0,Z_a^\sigma),&\text{with probability }1-\delta_T,
 \end{cases} \tag{7}
\]
where
\[
 Z_a^\sigma\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(
 \frac{1/2-\delta_Tr_a^\sigma}{1-\delta_T}\right). \tag{8}
\]
The probability in (8) lies in \([0,1]\).  For \(0\leq u\leq H_T\),
\[
 P\{D(a)>u\}=\delta_T\leq\frac L2(1+H_T)^{-\beta}
 \leq L(1+u)^{-\beta}, \tag{9}
\]
and the tail is zero for \(u\geq H_T+1\).  Thus the delay envelope holds.  Direct calculation gives
\[
 PY(a)=\frac12,qquad \operatorname{Var}_P\{Y(a)\}=\frac14, \tag{10}
\]
so \(\tau=0\).  The delayed component lies beyond \(h_{T,\Delta}\), enters neither correction, and yields
\[
 b_{T,\Delta}=\delta_T(r_1^\sigma-r_0^\sigma)=\sigma\delta_T. \tag{11}
\]
The quota formula gives
\[
 K_1(n_T)\sim\frac{c}{1-\alpha}T^{1-\alpha},
 \qquad K_0(n_T)\sim\varepsilon T. \tag{12}
\]
The visible Bernoulli probabilities tend to \(1/2\), so for some \(\gamma\in(0,\infty)\),
\[
 T^q s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow\gamma,
 \qquad
 \gamma^2=
 \begin{cases}
 (1-\alpha)/(4c),&\alpha>0,\\
 (c^{-1}+\varepsilon^{-1})/4,&\alpha=0.
 \end{cases} \tag{13}
\]
The second term in (6) is eventually active, whence
\[
 \frac{|b_{T,\Delta}|}{s_{T,\Delta}}
 =\frac{L}{2\gamma}x_T\{1+o(1)\}. \tag{14}
\]
For this fixed policy and bounded nondegenerate visible outcomes, the independent triangular-array argument used in \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}gated\text{-}inference}\) directly gives
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta}}
 {\widehat s_{T,\Delta}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
 \qquad \widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\to1. \tag{15}
\]
Along a subsequence on which (14) tends to \(u\in(0,\infty)\), the ordinary-Wald statistic converges to \(N(-\sigma u,1)\); its limiting coverage is
\[
 \Phi(z_{1-\eta/2}-u)+\Phi(z_{1-\eta/2}+u)-1<1-\eta. \tag{16}
\]
If (14) diverges, the centered term in (15) is tight while the shift diverges, so coverage tends to zero.  Every failure of \(x_T\to0\) has a subsequence of one of these kinds.  Therefore uniform honesty over the one-sided class requires
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\longrightarrow0. \tag{17}
\]
Conversely, \(\mathrm{prop:wald\text{-}followup\text{-}frontier}\) proves that (17) is sufficient on \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\).  Without the variance floor, (3)--(5) and the gated theorem give the stated uniformly honest alternatives.

It remains to solve (17).  If \(\Delta_T=0\) and \(\beta>q\), then
\[
 T^q(1+T)^{-\beta}=T^{q-\beta}\{1+o(1)\}\longrightarrow0. \tag{18}
\]
If \(\beta=q\),
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-q}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Delta_T/T\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{19}
\]
If \(\beta<q\), positivity and taking the \(\beta\)-th root give
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{T+\Delta_T}{T^{q/\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{20}
\]
Prompt-delay laws have \(b_{T,\Delta}=0\), so the obstruction is class-wide rather than pointwise.  The sampling converse uses prompt delays and is compatible with outcome--delay independence, whereas the hidden-tail witness (7) deliberately uses informative delay.
